activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today I am going to explain a routine but very important procedure in the Automobile Technology workshop.
This process is called brake bleeding.
We carry out this procedure to remove air from the brake system.
Please listen carefully and follow the sequence, because each step affects braking safety.
First, you have to check the brake fluid level in the master cylinder, because low fluid can allow air to enter the system.
Next, you should top up the brake fluid to the correct level so that the system remains full during bleeding.
After that, you have to position the vehicle safely and secure it using wheel chocks to prevent movement.
Then, it is important to identify the correct bleeding order so that air is removed efficiently.
You shouldn’t remove all four wheels at once, because this procedure is done one wheel at a time.
Proper preparation helps ensure accurate results and prevents fluid loss.
Once preparation is complete, you have to attach a clear hose to the bleed screw to observe air bubbles during bleeding.
Then, one technician has to press the brake pedal slowly, because sudden pressure can disturb the fluid flow.
At the same time, another technician needs to open the bleed screw slightly so that air and fluid can escape.
After that, you must tighten the bleed screw before releasing the pedal to stop air from re-entering the system.
You shouldn’t press the pedal too quickly, because slow and steady movement removes air more effectively.
This process is repeated until no air bubbles appear in the hose.
Finally, you have to refill the brake fluid reservoir to the correct level to maintain proper hydraulic pressure.
Then, you have to test the brake pedal firmness to confirm that the system works correctly.
You also need to inspect all bleed screws for leaks so that braking performance remains safe.
After that, clean any spilled brake fluid to protect painted surfaces.
You shouldn’t carry out a road test at this stage, because this session focuses only on the bleeding procedure.
Following this sequence ensures reliable braking and vehicle safety.
